uslaw-usc-t1-s6:
Section 6 of Title 1 of the United States Code trims the meaning of one trade phrase. The phrase is products of American fisheries, and it appears across federal statutes and agency rulings. This section declares what the term shall not include.

Excluded are fresh or frozen fish fillets, steaks, and slices of fish largely free of bone. The exclusion holds when those goods are produced in a foreign country or its territorial waters. It holds whether the foreign production is in whole or in part. A further condition is named: the work of persons who are not residents of the United States. Fish cut abroad by foreign labor, the section says, is no product of American fisheries. The definition guards a label used in tariff and fisheries law.
uslaw-usc-t2-s6:
Section 6 of Title 2 codifies a penalty on a State's representation for denying the vote. If a State denies or abridges the right of its male inhabitants, aged twenty-one and citizens, to vote at the elections named in the fourteenth amendment, a consequence follows. The number of Representatives apportioned to that State is reduced.

The reduction follows a stated proportion. It matches the share that the number of disenfranchised male citizens bears to the whole number of male citizens aged twenty-one in the State. An exception covers denial for participation in rebellion or for other crime. The section sits in Chapter 1 of Title 2, on the election of Senators and Representatives. Its terms track the second section of the fourteenth amendment itself. The hosted Code text is published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel, current through Public Law 119-134.
